newsitem.title: INDIA: Top official of India's Tamil Nadu dies.
newsitem.headline: Top official of India's Tamil Nadu dies.

text.p: A top official of India's southern state of Tamil Nadu died after a heart attack in Hyderabad early on Monday, his doctors said.

M. Chenna Reddy, 77, a veteran leader and governor of Tamil Nadu state, was taken to a nearby hospital when he complained of chest pain at around 3.00 a.m (2130 GMT). He died a few hours later, at 7.00 a.m. (0130 GMT), doctors at the hospital said.
Reddy, a doctor by profession, held many prestigious posts during a distinguished career. He was twice chief minister of Andhra Pradesh state, whose capital is Hyderabad, his hometown.
Reddy had served as federal junior minister for steel and mines in the government of former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi, assassinated by her own bodyguards in 1984.
Reddy was also a former governor of the northern states of Punjab, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh.
Both houses of India's parliament adjourned on Monday as a mark of respect to the veteran leader, the Press Trust of India newsagency reported.

Reddy led a violent movement for a separate state in Andhra Pradesh's Telangana region during 1969-71, which claimed at least 300 lives. A political settlement to the problem was worked out in 1973-74.
Reddy will be cremated with full state honours on Tuesday.
